purpose: Preserve dated evidence of Kerala's September 2026 supply stress for later stress-scenario calibration. These reports are not a substitute for SLDC interval telemetry or a fixed structural shortage assumption.

sources.attribution: Reports statements/data attributed to KSEB officials
Reports Kerala Power Department conservation circular

reported_conditions.interpretation: High energy demand did not imply a large peak shortage on this day because procurement/availability changed.

procurement_stress.note: Secondary reporting says private supply offers were extremely limited for September; this is market-availability evidence, not a permanent resource requirement.

Secondary reporting attributes part of the September stress to lower availability from central generating stations and long-/medium-term contracted sources, not solely to insufficient Kerala nameplate capacity.

interpretation_rules: Do not encode 700-900 MW as a permanent Kerala shortage. Reported shortfall varied from about 21 MW to more than 900 MW across individual days.
Do not infer that an 800 MW battery would remove the event; storage duration, charge availability, transmission, procurement and multi-day energy adequacy all matter.
Use this event to define stress scenarios only after matching exact SLDC/market/contract chronology.
The event demonstrates the importance of modeling external-supply availability and price jointly with demand, hydro and storage.
Media-reported values must be replaced or cross-checked with first-party SLDC/KSEBL/KSERC records before empirical calibration.

model_use.admissible_now: qualitative and bounded stress-scenario design only
model_use.desired_next_data: 15-minute demand, actual interchange, contracted/market supply, exchange prices, hydro generation and load-shedding/curtailment timestamps for September 2026
